S&P warns Nvidia's board may be compromised, puts chipmaker's rating on downgrade watch

S&P said it could downgrade Nvidia within the next 90 days, but expects any potential downgrade to be limited to one notch, unless investigations and other disclosures harm the company's reputation or future business prospects.

S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade on Wednesday (Nov 25), saying the departure and subsequent reinstatement of its CEO had exposed weaknesses in the chipmaker's management and board oversight . "We believe the long tenure of certain board members may have compromised their independence. The company's corporate governance practices may also not have kept pace with Nvidia's rapid growth and its role as a critical global technology enabler," the ratings agency said. The move comes amid a turbulent period for Nvidia's leadership. The company's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang earlier this week, days after he resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs with his direct reports as well as a Chinese businesswoman alleged by US intelligence to be Beijing's spy . Critics and lawmakers slammed the reinstatement, questioning the independence of the board, whose newly elected chair had told investors last week Nvidia would not rehire Huang as CEO because his personal behaviour was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct.

Reinstating Huang on Monday, Nvidia omitted any mention of his affairs, saying instead the move was "based on US government input", even as an independent board committee continued its investigation into reports involving him and a suspected foreign intelligence effort. Reuters reported on Wednesday that the US Justice Department did not conduct a formal investigation into Huang before US President Donald Trump pushed for his return as CEO, according to three people familiar with the matter. Instead, it concluded that there was no evidence he had broken any laws based on ongoing investigations into two Nvidia clients, Super Micro and Megaspeed International , which are suspected of smuggling advanced microchips to China. That determination is subject to change as the probes continue.

Related:

Jensen Huang’s stunning return as Nvidia CEO: A timeline of events

Inside the ‘war room’ that lobbied Donald Trump to bring back Nvidia’s Jensen Huang

NO EVIDENCE YET THAT ALICE HUANG IS A SPY Investors were largely unruffled by the S&P move, which comes with Nvidia shares down 38 per cent since Oct 6. Nvidia closed down nearly 4 per cent on Wednesday, retracing some declines after the Nasdaq 100 index briefly flirted with a 20 per cent decline from its recent high. The cost of insurance against tech companies defaulting on debts has jumped sharply in recent weeks, but the five-year CDS spread for Nvidia was little changed. Nvidia currently has an AA rating from S&P, which indicates a very strong capacity to meet financial commitments. The highest rating is AAA. The agency said it could downgrade Nvidia within the next 90 days, but expects any potential downgrade to be limited to one notch, unless investigations and other disclosures harm the company's reputation or future business prospects. Meanwhile, Moody's said on Wednesday that bringing back Huang eases near-term uncertainty around Nvidia's business execution and eliminates execution risk associated with appointing a new leader for the chipmaker. The agency said Nvidia's Aa1 rating and stable outlook remain unaffected, but added that governance and regulatory uncertainty persists.

WASHINGTON: Russia should avoid actions that expand its war in Ukraine, US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte said in a joint statement on Wednesday (Nov 26) after a meeting in Florida where they also discussed the Iran war. The meeting came after the Republican leader, who has been critical of America's Western allies, met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping last week in Asia, referring to each as his "friend." "We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible," the leaders said in their statement. Trump's meeting with Putin triggered a backlash from domestic Democratic opponents and European allies, with the latter having pushed to be included in US-backed talks to end the war in Ukraine.

Rutte, who has repeatedly tried to soothe tension within NATO and keep Trump onside, has said it was normal for major nuclear powers to meet. Rutte and Trump also talked about boosting defence spending and investment in the United States and across NATO, according to their statement. The war in Ukraine and US-Israeli war on Iran were the primary subjects of the talks, it added, but did not say what was discussed on Iran. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has been criticised by Trump, has said Europe had to be included in peace talks. Trump has often criticised Washington's Western and democratic allies over issues such as NATO spending, trade tariffs and what he calls their inadequate support for the war on Iran.

Elon Musk, the world's richest person, said on Wednesday (Nov 25) that every child in the US will receive two shares in SpaceX, the space and AI company he runs, pledging a gift worth some US$18 billion. Musk and rival AI company Anthropic have recently laid out sharply different blueprints for sharing some of the spoils of the AI boom, amid growing public and political scrutiny of the industry. Children will receive one share from the company and one from him personally, Musk said in a brief post on X, without providing details. In a separate post, Musk said the SpaceX shares will be transferred next month.

"The share directly from me will be transferred when my lockup expires in June next year," Musk added. SpaceX said earlier on Wednesday it would contribute one newly issued share of its Class A common stock to every currently active Trump Account, adding that Musk will personally match the number of shares donated by the company. A Trump Account is a program designed to give Americans under the age of 18 a stake in the stock market and help build wealth from an early age. The White House said in October it had opened almost 70 million accounts. SpaceX shares closed at US$127.44 on Wednesday, valuing the pledge at nearly US$18 billion.

SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether Musk's SpaceX share donations would be linked to Trump Accounts. "What it does is build a massive, long-term retail shareholder base," said Christopher Brankin, global markets advisor at brokerage Mitrade Group. "It builds immediate market engagement and creates a massive, financially literate client pipeline for trading platforms as that generation comes of age." Musk, whose net worth is around US$824 billion, said last month he would give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in America. He held about 6.42 billion shares in the company as of June. "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," Musk said in a post on X at the time. "Giving shares, which are stakes in the future economy, directly to the people is the way," Musk added. Most of Musk's philanthropic efforts have been through the Musk Foundation, which reportedly holds more than US$14 billion in assets.

In October, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband pledged a share of their SpaceX stock to each of more than 2 million children under the Trump initiative. Anthropic, which recently went public, said last month it was committing 5 per cent of its shares to a new fund for the "public good". It said that the initiative, worth around US$54 billion at current prices, will give it more flexibility and scale to make donations for the benefit of humanity. Other executives have also set up major, long-running philanthropy ventures. Berkshire Hathaway Chairman Emeritus Warren Buffett, one of the most prominent figures in philanthropy, is reported to have given away US$60 billion so far, with most of the rest of his roughly US$150 billion fortune slated for philanthropy too. The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has distributed more than US$100 billion since its founding in 2000, with some of that fueled by donations from Buffett.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported nine measles-related deaths in the United States this year, as the country battles its worst outbreak of the highly contagious viral infection in decades. The US had recorded 6,039 confirmed measles cases as of Nov 24, across 47 jurisdictions, according to the agency's website on Wednesday. That includes 18 cases among international visitors. The CDC updated its tally after the National Center for Health Statistics received additional reports from states and verified that the deaths had occurred and that measles was the underlying cause, a Department of Health and Human Services spokesperson said. Based on publicly reported state figures, however, the US has recorded at least 14 measles-associated deaths this year, including nine fatalities in Pennsylvania, three in Wisconsin and one each in Virginia and New York state.

A discrepancy between state and federal death tallies arose earlier this year after CDC, under US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures. "The discrepancy between state and federal measles-related death figures is concerning and risks confusing the public about the true toll of this outbreak," said Frederic Bertley, immunologist and CEO of the Center of Science and Industry. "Regardless of the precise number, these deaths are alarming and reflect the consequences of declining vaccination coverage," Bertley said. Cases in the US have reached a 35-year high, a resurgence driven largely by unvaccinated people that this month stripped the country of its hard-fought measles elimination status . CDC data showed that 671 patients, or 11 per cent of confirmed cases, were hospitalised, with children aged under 5 years recording the highest hospitalisation rate at 17 per cent. The agency also said the death count could change as it reviews additional information. On Wednesday, Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit US state, reported 1,679 measles cases so far this year, including 87 new cases over the past seven days and 340 hospitalisations.

Israeli judges recommend prosecutors drop one bribery case against Netanyahu

Israeli judges have recommended dropping one of three corruption cases against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and reconsidering another, in a trial that began in 2020.

JERUSALEM: Israeli judges on Wednesday (Nov 25) recommended that prosecutors drop one of three long-running cases against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and reconsider another alleging he granted favours in exchange for positive media coverage. Netanyahu was indicted in 2019 on charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust. He denies the charges and has pleaded not guilty. His trial began in 2020 and involves three criminal cases. In the case referred to as Case 4000, prosecutors allege that Netanyahu granted regulatory favours worth around 1.8 billion shekels (about US$500 million) to Bezeq Telecom Israel. In return, prosecutors say, he sought positive coverage for himself and his wife, Sara, on a news website controlled by former Bezeq Chairman Shaul Elovitch. Elovitch has denied wrongdoing. In a blow to prosecutors, Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman of Jerusalem District Court , who presides over Case 4000, told Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara at a hearing on Wednesday that a conviction was unlikely and the case should be dropped.

The recommendation was not a ruling on the case, the court clarified, and Baharav-Miara said she would review the court's statements with the prosecution. The judges also recommended prosecutors reconsider so-called Case 2000 because of doubts that Netanyahu's actions constituted a criminal offence. In that case, prosecutors allege Netanyahu negotiated a deal with Arnon Mozes, owner of Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper, for better coverage in return for legislation to slow the growth of a rival newspaper. Netanyahu on Wednesday called the court's recommendation a "ray of light for truth and justice." "Ten years of suffering for dozens of my close ones who were dragged into interrogation rooms," Netanyahu said in a televised address. "Where they were blackmailed with criminal acts, humiliated, and the lives of many of them were ruined, just so they would give false testimony against me."

BERLIN: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz accused Russia on Wednesday (Nov 25) of "escalating" threats to European security as he defended his government's plans to bolster defence spending and maintain financial aid to Ukraine. Opposition parties, including t he far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), which tops national opinion polls, and t he hard-left Die Linke, have called for an end to military aid to Kyiv . "It cannot be s aid often enough, against t he far right as much as t he far left: Russia knows exactly what it wants . And Russia wants more than Ukraine," Merz told t he Bundestag lower house of parliament during a debate on t he 2027 draft budget. "Russia is escalating in t he Baltic region, in Poland, on t he Black Sea; Russia is escalating in space, and Russia is by now also escalating massively he re in our own country," he s aid .

Russia did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on Merz 's accusations. It has repeatedly denied seeking military confrontation with NATO countries and says its actions in Ukraine are aimed at protecting its own national security. Merz 's government blamed Russia in September for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle airport , an accusation t he Russian Embassy in Berlin dismissed as part of a "new wave of anti-Russian hysteria in Germany". Germany and ot he r European countries have also been hit by a wave of cyberattacks and sabotage incidents targeting critical infrastructure that t he y have often blamed on Russia. Moscow has denied all t he allegations.

"LEARNING FROM UKRAINE" Merz s aid on Wednesday that by supporting Ukraine, Germany was also protecting itself. "We are learning from Ukraine - technologically for civilian use but of course also in defence technology," he s aid . Germany has been Ukraine's biggest military backer in Europe since Russia's full-blown invasion on Feb 24, 2022, but public support for this policy has decreased amid cost-of-living pressures. A poll publis he d on Tuesday showed a narrow majority of Germans now oppose giving military aid to Kyiv . "Whose chancellor are you, actually?" AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla asked Merz during Wednesday's debate, accusing the government of supporting Ukraine while failing to provide sufficient relief to German citizens. "What a mockery!" Germany aims to double defence spending to over €200 billion (US$228 billion) between now and 2030, according to t he 2027 draft budget, hitting 3.7 per cent of national output by 2030, in line with commitments to NATO.

EU SHOULD FOCUS ON SECURITY AND COMPETITIVENESS, MERZ SAYS Merz also addressed on Wednesday t he latest proposal for t he European Union budget for 2028-2034 presented by European Council chief Antonio Costa. Costa proposed cuts that would reduce t he overall seven-year budget to €1.582 trillion, some €40 billion less than a proposal presented by t he Irish EU presidency in October. EU leaders will discuss Costa's proposals at a special summit on Thursday and Friday. "In t he se negotiations I am pushing for spending to be limited and focused on what really makes Europe stronger: security and competitiveness," Merz s aid . "If spending is focused, it is t he best additional insurance for our country."
